text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Constitutional Council may announce on Thursday its decisions on 19 appeals by defeated candidates in last summer's parliamentary elections, or it may postpone them.
- Maronite Patriarch Sfeir said: "The Pope will raise the issue of Lebanon's) sovereignty during his visit". Pope John Paul II will arrive in Beirut on May 10 for a two-day visit.
- Beirut Chamber of Commerce and Industry and other economic associations prepare a study of country's economic problems.
- Unemployment reached 15 percent in 1995 with 165,000 unemployed.
- Lawyers of Samir Geagea, Christian warlord serving three life sentences for murder, send the Pope an open letter explaining his situation.
- Russian ambassador Peressypkine said his country will sign cultural agreements with Lebanon.
